subject: tilted apartment buildings
title: What If the Ground Turned Liquid? In 1964 Whole Buildings Tipped Over

scenes.text: What if the ground under your building turned to liquid? In 1964, Niigata, Japan found out.
June 16th, 1964. A magnitude 7.6 quake hits. Along the Shinano River, apartment blocks on reclaimed land start to lean.
The sand underneath is soaked. Shaking makes the grains lose contact, and for a few moments the ground behaves like a liquid.
Most of the blocks tilt; one topples completely, in one piece, with remarkably little structural damage.
Sand volcanoes erupt across the city, exactly where old maps show buried rivers. The ground sinks up to 1.4 meters.
Seventy seconds in, the Showa Bridge drops into the river as the liquid ground spreads. Christchurch learned the same lesson in 2011.

description:
What if the ground under your building turned to liquid? On 16 June 1964 a magnitude 7.6 earthquake hit Niigata, Japan. Water-soaked sand under apartment blocks on reclaimed land liquefied: most of the blocks tilted and one toppled over in one piece with little structural damage. Sand volcanoes erupted where old maps showed buried river channels, the ground subsided by up to 1.4 meters, and about 70 seconds in, the Showa Bridge collapsed as the ground spread sideways.
Liquefaction needs loose wet sediment and strong shaking; it also caused much of the damage in Christchurch in 2011 (USGS).

first_comment: Niigata was already sinking about 20 centimeters a year before the quake because of groundwater pumping. Is your city built on old riverbed or reclaimed land? And what should we run through next?
